niche.title: The Oldest Brain Surgery Was Better Than Civil War Medicine
niche.description:
Bone grows back around a hole in the skull only if the person lived for months. That one detail rewrites everything we assume about ancient surgery.

Studies of Neolithic and Bronze Age skulls put survival around 72% and higher — while early medieval survival sat near 50%. Nearly 800 Peruvian skulls show Inca-era survival above 75%.

Would you trust the flint, or the scalpel that came after it?

Kostiantyn "Magura" Vlasenko, 49, of the 30th Brigade spent nearly 500 days at his post; mines and enemy drones blocked any ground evacuation.
